accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Narasapuram was known for the export of cheap calico. White cloth came from Injaram, rumaals from Nellore and indigo from Nagulavancha and Nalgonda.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate the swapped export centres.
accepted.sec: Exports from coastal Andhra → centre; dominant pre-colonial industry

accepted.s: White cloth known as ‘taanis’ was exported from which centre of coastal Andhra?
accepted.x: Injaram was associated with the export of white cloth known as taanis.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of a specific commodity-centre association.
accepted.sec: Exports from coastal Andhra → centre; dominant pre-colonial industry

accepted.s: Rumaals, or handkerchiefs, were an export associated with which place?
accepted.x: Nellore was known for the export of rumaals or handkerchiefs.
accepted.tq: Direct commodity-to-place recall.
accepted.sec: Exports from coastal Andhra → centre; dominant pre-colonial industry

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Saltpetre — Machilipatnam, Narsapur and Pulicat
2. Diamonds — Golconda mines and Kollur
3. Indigo — Nagulavancha and Nalgonda
4. Salt — Pedaganjam and Chinaganjam
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correct. Saltpetre was exported from Machilipatnam, Narsapur and Pulicat; diamonds came from Golconda and Kollur; indigo from Nagulavancha and Nalgonda; and salt from Pedaganjam and Chinaganjam.
accepted.tq: Check each commodity against its centre before selecting the comprehensive combination.
accepted.sec: Exports from coastal Andhra → centre; dominant pre-colonial industry

accepted.s: The Koh-i-Noor diamond was associated with which mining area of coastal Andhra?
accepted.x: Kollur in Guntur was associated with the Koh-i-Noor, while diamonds were also obtained from the Golconda mines.
accepted.tq: Numerical-place and famous-object discrimination.
accepted.sec: Exports from coastal Andhra → centre; dominant pre-colonial industry

accepted.s: Which industry was dominant in the pre-colonial economy of the region and ranked second only to diamonds in the Qutb Shahi economy?
accepted.x: Textiles were the dominant pre-colonial industry and stood second only to diamonds in the Qutb Shahi economy.
accepted.tq: Direct identification of the dominant sector from a comparison.
accepted.sec: Exports from coastal Andhra → centre; dominant pre-colonial industry

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT listed as an additional export of coastal Andhra?
accepted.x: Carpets, iron, steel, swords, lacquer toys, leather, footwear, sesame, castor, sugar and wax were listed as other exports. Tea was not included.
accepted.tq: Find the outsider in a group of regionally associated exports.
accepted.sec: Exports from coastal Andhra → centre; dominant pre-colonial industry

accepted.s: Which of the following groups contains only textile ports that shipped goods to England, France and Holland?
accepted.x: Kalingapatnam, Srikakulam, Vizag and Bhimunipatnam were among the textile ports shipping to England, France and Holland. The other options combine mining, salt, inland or other trade centres.
accepted.tq: Recognise the complete regional list rather than a single familiar port.
accepted.sec: Exports from coastal Andhra → centre; dominant pre-colonial industry

accepted.s: Under whose control did Masulipatnam serve as the principal maritime gateway of the Sultanate?
accepted.x: Under the Qutb Shahis of Golconda, Masulipatnam was the Sultanate’s main maritime gateway, and its customs revenue contributed to Golconda’s wealth.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler-and-port association; avoid swapping neighbouring dynasties.
accepted.sec: Masulipatnam - ruler controlling the port, merchant communities, textiles

accepted.s: In which year did Aurangzeb annex Golconda, after which Masulipatnam passed to the Mughals?
accepted.x: Aurangzeb annexed Golconda in 1687, and Masulipatnam subsequently passed under Mughal control.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the closely spaced dates associated with European factories and Mughal conquest.
accepted.sec: Masulipatnam - ruler controlling the port, merchant communities, textiles

accepted.s: Which merchant community played the key role in the trade of Masulipatnam?
accepted.x: The Komatis played the key role among the merchant communities of Masulipatnam.
accepted.tq: Direct community-to-port recall.
accepted.sec: Masulipatnam - ruler controlling the port, merchant communities, textiles

accepted.s: The weaving groups associated with Masulipatnam were known as:
accepted.x: Mughra and Theliyaneta were the weaving groups associated with Masulipatnam.
accepted.tq: Confusable-name discrimination among communities and textile terms.
accepted.sec: Masulipatnam - ruler controlling the port, merchant communities, textiles

accepted.s: Approximately how many weavers worked for the Dutch at Masulipatnam and were paid in Madras pagodas?
accepted.x: About 5,000 weavers worked for the Dutch at Masulipatnam and received payment in Madras pagodas.
accepted.tq: Recall the distinctive quantitative detail and reject nearby rounded figures.
accepted.sec: Masulipatnam - ruler controlling the port, merchant communities, textiles

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the textile terms associated with Masulipatnam is correct?
o: Chintz was glazed and became brighter after washing.
Palampores were a type of saltpetre.
Kalamkari denoted a European coin used to pay weavers.
Pintado referred exclusively to plain white cloth.
accepted.x: Chintz was glazed and became brighter after washing. Pintado, palampores and kalamkari were also associated with Masulipatnam textiles, but the other descriptions are incorrect.
accepted.tq: Separate closely related textile names by their precise descriptions.
accepted.sec: Masulipatnam - ruler controlling the port, merchant communities, textiles

accepted.s: Why did the English bans on calico in 1700 and 1721 not seriously damage Andhra’s textile trade?
o: Other markets remained open to Andhra textiles.
The Qutb Shahis subsidised all calico exports.
The Dutch stopped exporting textiles from Andhra.
Andhra textiles were exempt from all European regulations.
accepted.x: The bans imposed by England in 1700 and 1721 did not seriously affect Andhra because other markets remained open.
accepted.tq: Link the policy measure with its stated economic consequence.
accepted.sec: Masulipatnam - ruler controlling the port, merchant communities, textiles

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Masulipatnam lighthouses in chronological order from earliest to latest:
A. Lighthouse near Manginapudi
B. Lighthouse at Tavisipudi
C. Lighthouse at Campbelpeta
accepted.x: The earlier lighthouse was at Tavisipudi in 1858, followed by Campbelpeta in 1903, while the present lighthouse near Manginapudi dates from 1984.
accepted.tq: Use the first and last dates to fix the sequence before placing the middle item.
accepted.sec: Masulipatnam - ruler controlling the port, merchant communities, textiles

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding shipbuilding in coastal Andhra?
o: Bheemunipatnam — major shipbuilding centre in the stated period
accepted.x: Narasapuram and Machilipatnam built ships and boats. Corangi was a shipbuilding site in the Company era; shipbuilding at Nizampatnam and Bheemunipatnam was specifically excluded.
accepted.tq: Identify the supported association while rejecting unsupported port claims.
accepted.sec: Shipbuilding centres of coastal Andhra

accepted.s: Sea-going ships were referred to as which of the following in the Shuka Saptati?
accepted.x: The term odaberam was used for sea-going ships in the Shuka Saptati.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of a specialised historical term.
accepted.sec: Shipbuilding centres of coastal Andhra

accepted.s: Which of the following sequences correctly arranges the establishment of the specified European factories from earlier to later?
o: Dutch at Masulipatnam — English at Masulipatnam — French at Masulipatnam — French at Yanam
English at Masulipatnam — Dutch at Masulipatnam — French at Masulipatnam — French at Yanam
Dutch at Masulipatnam — French at Masulipatnam — English at Masulipatnam — French at Yanam
French at Masulipatnam — Dutch at Masulipatnam — English at Masulipatnam — French at Yanam
accepted.x: The Dutch established their Masulipatnam factory in 1605, the English in 1611, the French in 1669, and the French presence at Yanam dates from 1723.
accepted.tq: Fix the sequence by comparing the factory years rather than the European powers.
accepted.sec: Trade centres → European power + factory year

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Dutch established a factory at Pulicat in 1610. The English factory at Vizagapatnam dates from 1682, the French presence at Yanam from 1723, and the English factory at Masulipatnam from 1611.
accepted.tq: Match each centre with both the correct European power and year.
accepted.sec: Trade centres → European power + factory year

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Dutch established a factory at Pulicat in 1610.
2. The English established a factory at Pulicat in 1621.
3. The English established a factory at Vizagapatnam in 1682.
4. The French established a factory at Yanam in 1723.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct according to the recorded European factory dates for Pulicat, Vizagapatnam and Yanam.
accepted.tq: Verify each date independently before choosing the all-inclusive code.
accepted.sec: Trade centres → European power + factory year

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Madapollam was associated with the English, not the French. Nizampatnam had Dutch and English connections, Bheemunipatnam had Dutch and English factories, and Palakollu had a Dutch factory.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong European-power association rather than the missing-year distractor.
accepted.sec: Trade centres → European power + factory year

accepted.s: Which financial resource from Europe financed English purchases of chintz, calico and muslin?
accepted.x: Bullion brought from Europe financed English purchases of chintz, calico and muslin.
accepted.tq: Directly connect the financial input with the commodities purchased.
accepted.sec: Imports into Andhra ports - commodities and source regions

accepted.s: Horses reaching Andhra ports were brought mainly through which traders?
accepted.x: Horses came through Portuguese and Arab traders.
accepted.tq: Identify the source traders associated with a specific imported commodity.
accepted.sec: Imports into Andhra ports - commodities and source regions

accepted.s: What did the Dutch commonly exchange for Coromandel textiles?
accepted.x: The Dutch traded Coromandel textiles in exchange for spices from the East Indies.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the traded commodity from the financing medium and transport goods.
accepted.sec: Imports into Andhra ports - commodities and source regions

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT included among the colonial-era imports into Andhra ports?
accepted.x: Colonial-era imports included metals, minerals, porcelain, liquor, drugs, iron, steel and medicines. Kalamkari was an Andhra textile export, not an import in this list.
accepted.tq: Separate an export textile from the listed colonial imports.
accepted.sec: Imports into Andhra ports - commodities and source regions

accepted.s: During the Company era, small boats carried salt and groceries to Yanam, Bengal, Rangoon and Chittagong and returned with:
accepted.x: The boats returned with rice and grains after carrying salt and groceries to the listed destinations.
accepted.tq: Track the direction of movement and avoid reversing exports and imports.
accepted.sec: Imports into Andhra ports - commodities and source regions

accepted.s: Which statement regarding Yanam is correct?
o: It was the only French territorial possession in the Andhra region.
It was the principal Dutch headquarters in India from 1690.
It became an English possession in 1954.
It lies outside the Union Territory of Puducherry.
accepted.x: Yanam was the French power’s only territorial possession in the Andhra region. It merged into the Indian Union in 1954 and is now part of Puducherry.
accepted.tq: Use the ownership and present-status distinctions to reject swapped powers and territories.
accepted.sec: Yanam - European owner, merger, present status

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the constitutional and territorial status of Yanam?
o: It merged into the Indian Union in 1723 and is now part of Tamil Nadu.
It was transferred de facto in 1962 and is now a district of Andhra Pradesh.
It merged into the Indian Union in 1954 and is now an enclave of Puducherry in the Godavari delta.
It was transferred to France in 1954 and remains a French overseas territory.
accepted.x: Yanam merged into the Indian Union in 1954, while the de jure transfer occurred in 1962. It is presently an enclave of the Union Territory of Puducherry in Andhra Pradesh’s Godavari delta.
accepted.tq: Separate merger, de jure transfer and present territorial status.
accepted.sec: Yanam - European owner, merger, present status

accepted.s: Bhimili, or Bheemunipatnam, became the first municipality in Andhra in which year?
accepted.x: Bhimili became the first municipality in Andhra in 1861.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the municipality year from the nearby lighthouse and merger years.
accepted.sec: Bheemunipatnam - surviving European-period monuments

accepted.s: Which European-period monument survives at Bheemunipatnam?
accepted.x: A Dutch cemetery survives at Bheemunipatnam. The place also had a Dutch subordinate factory that later became an English factory.
accepted.tq: Direct identification of a surviving monument and its European association.
accepted.sec: Bheemunipatnam - surviving European-period monuments

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Bheemunipatnam:
1. It had a Dutch subordinate factory.
2. The factory later became an English factory.
3. Bhimili became the first municipality in Andhra in 1861.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Bheemunipatnam had a Dutch subordinate factory, later an English factory, and Bhimili became Andhra’s first municipality in 1861.
accepted.tq: Combine institutional succession with a precise municipal date.
accepted.sec: Bheemunipatnam - surviving European-period monuments

accepted.s: Which port was an important Kakatiya port where Ganapatideva’s Abhaya Sasanam protected foreign traders?
accepted.x: Motupalli was an important Kakatiya port, and Ganapatideva’s Abhaya Sasanam protected foreign traders there.
accepted.tq: Associate the royal inscription and its protection of foreign traders with the correct port.
accepted.sec: Other historic ports and centres

accepted.s: Who issued another sea-trade-related record associated with the Reddi period?
accepted.x: Somaya, a minister of the Reddi period, issued another record concerning sea trade.
accepted.tq: Avoid swapping the Kakatiya ruler with the Reddi-period minister.
accepted.sec: Other historic ports and centres

accepted.s: Nagapattinam served as the headquarters of which European power in India from 1690?
accepted.x: Nagapattinam was the Dutch headquarters in India from 1690.
accepted.tq: Match the port, European power and starting year.
accepted.sec: Other historic ports and centres

accepted.s: Which pair consists of ancient east-coast ports associated with the Satavahana period?
accepted.x: Ghantasala, also called Kantakasela, and Koddura were ancient east-coast ports associated with the Satavahana period.
accepted.tq: Use the dynasty-period association to distinguish ancient ports from later centres.
accepted.sec: Other historic ports and centres

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT listed as a major post-European trade centre?
accepted.x: Kondapalli, Golconda, Narsapur and Madras were listed as major post-European trade centres. Srikurmam was identified as a pilgrim centre that grew into a trade centre, not in this post-European list.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the post-European list from the separate pilgrim-centre list.
accepted.sec: Other historic ports and centres

accepted.s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of pilgrim centres that later grew into trade centres?
accepted.x: Tirupati, Srisailam, Srikurmam and Srikalahasti were pilgrim centres that developed into trade centres.
accepted.tq: Recognise the complete thematic group and reject mixed port lists.
accepted.sec: Other historic ports and centres
